Six of Rajasthan's hill forts are inscribed together as a World Heritage Site. The tour examines how the forts were sited, supplied with water and defended, with a historian accompanying the group throughout.

A day-by-day itinerary and a quotation are shared before you commit. Route, pace, accommodation and budget are adjusted to suit your group.

What it covers

  • Forts chosen with you from the six on the World Heritage list: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer
  • How each was sited, supplied with water and defended
  • A historian with the group throughout

Day by day

  1. Day 1: Jaipur

    Arrival, and an introduction to how and why Rajasthan's forts were built where they are.

  2. Day 2: Amber and Jaigarh

    A palace-fort and the fortress above it: defence, water supply and court life.

  3. Day 3: To Chittorgarh

    A long road day, broken with a stop on the way.

  4. Day 4: Chittorgarh

    The largest of the hill forts: gates, reservoirs, palaces and towers.

  5. Day 5: To Kumbhalgarh

    The drive through the Aravalli hills, and the fort walls at dusk.

  6. Day 6: Kumbhalgarh

    The walls, the gateways and the temples inside them.

  7. Days 7 and 8: Udaipur, or an extension

    Departure from Udaipur, or on to Ranthambore, Gagron or Jaisalmer to complete the set of six.

Days can be added, removed or reordered. The final itinerary comes with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Explain how Rajasthan's hill forts were sited, supplied with water and defended.
  • Identify the gates, reservoirs, palaces and towers of Chittorgarh, the largest of the hill forts.
  • Describe defence, water supply and court life at the palace-fort of Amber and Jaigarh above it.

You take away

Daily field sheets and a final comparative portfolio.
